findings.title: i.content can be nil, crashing the hourly feed job
findings.body: In poll_feed, `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every feed item has a `content` element. Plain RSS 2.0 feeds typically only have `description`, not `content`, so SimpleRSS will return nil and `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError, aborting the entire feed poll (and because `sidekiq_options retry: false`, nothing is retried and no items from that feed are imported until the next hour, which will crash the same way). Use `i.content || i.description` and guard for nil.

findings.title: raw_html cook method stores and serves completely unsanitized HTML
findings.body: `cook` returns `raw` verbatim when cook_method is :raw_html, so posts imported via TopicEmbed.import (feed polling or remote retrieval of the embeddable host) bypass PrettyText/Sanitize entirely and are served as-is (the embed view even does `raw post.cooked`). Any script/event-handler markup in a fetched article or feed item becomes stored XSS on the forum itself, visible in topic pages, digests, and embeds. The imported HTML should be run through Sanitize with an allowlist before storage.

findings.title: postMessage origin check uses substring match
findings.body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that merely appears as a substring of discourseUrl. An origin like `https://evil.com/redirect?https://forum.example.com` would pass if discourseUrl is configured correspondingly, and more simply the check never validates that e.origin actually equals the forum's origin. Any site able to get a message to the parent window can resize the iframe; the check should compare e.origin against a parsed expected origin.

findings.title: Check-then-create on embed_url races and raises RecordNotUnique
findings.body: import() does `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and then `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction. The migration adds a unique index on embed_url, so two concurrent imports of the same URL (hourly PollFeed plus a RetrieveTopic job enqueued from embed#best, which explicitly runs PollFeed and then fetches HTTP itself) will both find no row and one will crash with ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique. Rescue RecordNotUnique and fall back to the update path, or use an upsert.

findings.title: absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs
findings.body: Any href/src starting with '/' is prefixed with the article's scheme+host. Protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x.jpg` start with '/', so they are rewritten to `http://host/cdn.example.com/x.jpg`, breaking those links/images in every imported post. Check for a leading '//' and skip (or prepend only the scheme) before treating the URL as host-relative.

findings.title: feed_key is dead code; job does no change detection
findings.body: feed_key computes a redis key 'feed-modified:<sha>' but nothing ever reads or writes it, and poll_feed re-downloads the feed and re-hashes/re-imports every item every hour. Either wire the key up to skip unchanged feeds (e.g. via If-Modified-Since/ETag or content hash) or remove it; as-is every hourly run re-fetches all items and calls PostRevisor/sha comparisons for each.

findings.title: Editing an already-shipped migration to add force: true
findings.body: CreateTopTopics already ran in existing deployments; changing `create_table :top_topics` to `force: true` modifies history. Environments that haven't run it yet (or that replay migrations, e.g. some CI/staging rebuilds after a partially applied state) will silently DROP and recreate the top_topics table, losing all aggregated counts. New behavior should go in a new migration rather than editing an old one.

findings.title: X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL is non-standard and unsupported
findings.body: `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = 'ALLOWALL'` is not a valid X-Frame-Options value (ALLOW-FROM requires a URI and is unsupported in Chrome/Safari; ALLOWALL is ignored entirely by most browsers). The effect is only achieved because an invalid value happens to be ignored — better to explicitly remove the header so the intent is clear and future middleware adding a default DENY doesn't break embeds.

findings.title: import mutates the caller's contents string
findings.body: `contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends the 'imported from' footer directly to the string passed in. Callers that reuse the buffer (e.g. the Readability document content or anything comparing the original afterwards) get silently modified data, and the sha1 is computed over the mutated value. Duplicate the string (`contents = contents + ...` or `contents.dup`) before appending.

findings.title: Throws if #discourse-comments element is missing
findings.body: `comments.appendChild(iframe)` runs without checking that `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` found an element. Site owners paste this snippet into arbitrary templates; if the container is absent or renamed, the script throws and no iframe is created, with no useful error. Bail out early (or log a clear message) when comments is null.
